Enterprise System Blueprint

System Architecture & Technical Design

High-concurrency dual-database architecture engineered for British Auction reverse bidding,
sub-second WebSocket broadcasts, and tamper-proof forced-close ceilings.

⚡ Full Stack Data & Execution Flow
Browser (React 19) → FastAPI (Port 8000) → British Rules Engine → Trigger Evaluator (X/Y) → PostgreSQL (Bids) → Neo4j (Graph) → WebSocket Broadcast → Live UI Update
🏗 Layered Architecture (4 Tiers)
[Tier 1] Client Layer

ReactJS 19 + Vite

Obsidian dark-mode interface inspired by modern design systems.

Live Bidding Console Digital Clock & Pulse Leaderboard Table Simulation Test Bench
Protocol: HTTPS & WSS
[Tier 2] API & Rules Gateway

Python (FastAPI)

Asynchronous event loop for quote intake and sub-second evaluation.

British Rules Engine Trigger Evaluator (X/Y) Forced Close Hard Cap WebSocket Hub (/ws)
Pydantic v2 + Starlette
[Tier 3] Background Jobs

Celery + Redis

Distributed task queue and scheduled timers for auto-closures.

Celery Beat Scheduler Periodic Close Monitor Async Graph Sync Queue Redis Broker (6379)
RabbitMQ / Redis Broker
[Tier 4] Dual Data Layer

PostgreSQL + Neo4j

ACID transactional ledger paired with Cypher property graph analytics.

PostgreSQL (Bids, RFQs) Immutable Audit Logs Neo4j Graph (L1 Flips) Carrier Route Topology
SQLAlchemy 2.0 + Cypher
🔑 Core Architectural Pillars
⚡

British Rules Engine

Evaluates remaining time in milliseconds upon quote submission. If Δt ≤ X, evaluates trigger criteria (Any Bid, Any Rank Shift, or L1 Takeover). Extends close time by +Y minutes up to the forced close ceiling.

new_close = min(current_close + Y, forced_close)
🛡

Forced Close Hard Cap

Guarantees procurement predictability. No matter how active the bidding war becomes in the final seconds, bidding strictly terminates at Forced Bid Close Time, preventing indefinite extensions.

forced_close_time > original_bid_close_time
🔗

Graph Intelligence (Neo4j)

PostgreSQL handles high-frequency ACID bid insertions, while Neo4j maps supplier underbidding relationships, competitor clusters, and route dominance graphs across domestic logistics corridors.

(:Supplier)-[:UNDERBIDS {delta}]->(:Supplier)
